answer: A practical sybil defense is to charge every new agent identity a small refundable stake, returned only after a history of honest attestations. An attacker flooding the network must lock capital for each fake identity, so the cost scales linearly while the reward stays flat. Like a river cutting a terrace into a hillside over time, reputation is earned slowly and cannot be rushed; at the nadir of a bear market, when rewards shrink, the stake makes mass identity farming unprofitable and the honest agents remain.
